recipes.name: Split Pea Soup with Ham
recipes.summary: A thick, smoky pot of green split peas, carrots and diced ham. It tastes even better the next day.

ingredients.prep: low-sodium if you can find it

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery 6 to 8 minutes, until soft. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.

Add the split peas, ham, broth, water, thyme, bay leaf and pepper. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, partly cover and simmer 60 to 75 minutes, stirring now and then so the peas do not stick, until they fall apart.
Pull out the thyme stems and bay leaf. For a smoother soup, mash some of the peas against the side of the pot. Taste, then add salt only if needed; the ham is salty.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. It thickens as it sits; thin with water and reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze in portions for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Pack it hot in an insulated food jar for lunch.

recipes.kids: Serve with buttered toast or crackers for dipping.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the ham and broth labels.
swaps.meatless: Skip the ham, use vegetable broth and add 1 teaspoon smoked paprika.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the soup; it reheats well all week.

recipes.name: Yellow Split Pea Dal
recipes.summary: Golden split peas simmered soft with turmeric, then finished with onion, garlic, ginger and cumin. Mild enough for kids.
recipes.serving_size: about 1 cup dal with 3/4 cup rice
steps: Put the split peas, 5 cups water and turmeric in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then simmer partly covered 40 to 45 minutes, stirring often, until the peas are very soft. Add water if it gets too thick.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice, then simmer it covered in 2 1/4 cups water for 15 minutes. Let it stand off the heat 10 minutes.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 8 minutes, until golden. Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander and cayenne for 1 minute.
Stir the onion mixture, tomatoes and salt into the peas and simmer 5 minutes. Add the lemon juice and cilantro. Serve over the rice.
recipes.make_ahead: The dal keeps 4 days in the fridge and thickens; loosen it with water when you reheat it to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze the dal (not the rice) for up to 3 months.

leftovers.text: Spoon leftover dal into a warm tortilla or naan for lunch.

recipes.kids: Leave out the cayenne and set out plain yogurt to cool each bite.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the dal; make rice fresh or freeze it in portions.

recipes.name: Greek Yellow Split Pea Dip (Fava)
recipes.summary: A smooth, lemony spread made from yellow split peas, the way it is served in Greece. Eat it warm or cold with pita.

ingredients.prep: plus a little for the top

steps: Put the split peas, onion, garlic and water in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim the foam, then simmer partly covered 40 to 50 minutes, stirring now and then, until very soft and most of the water is absorbed.
Cool 10 minutes. Blend with the olive oil, lemon juice and salt until smooth. It thickens as it cools; blend in warm water a spoonful at a time if needed.
Spread in a shallow bowl. Top with red onion, parsley, capers if you like and a drizzle of oil.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 5 days in the fridge. Stir before serving.

freezer.text: Freeze without the topping for up to 2 months; it may need a stir and a splash of water after thawing.

leftovers.text: Spread it in a wrap with cucumbers and tomatoes.

recipes.kids: Serve with carrot sticks and pita; it tastes a lot like hummus.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve with vegetables or gluten-free crackers instead of pita.

prep_day.ahead: Make the dip for snacks and lunches.

recipes.name: Split Pea and Barley Vegetable Soup
recipes.summary: A hearty meatless soup of green split peas, pearl barley and vegetables. Thick, cheap and filling.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery 8 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, thyme and paprika for 30 seconds.
Add the split peas, barley, broth, water, bay leaf and pepper. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered 60 to 70 minutes, stirring now and then, until the peas break down and the barley is tender.
Remove the bay leaf, stir in the parsley and taste for salt. Add water if it is thicker than you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 5 days in the fridge; thin with water as you reheat it to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months.

leftovers.text: Heat a mug for an after-school snack or pack it for lunch.

recipes.kids: Top each bowl with a few oyster crackers or shredded cheese.

swaps.gluten_free: Use brown rice instead of barley and add it for the last 40 minutes.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the soup.

recipes.name: Curried Split Pea and Sweet Potato Soup
recipes.summary: Yellow split peas and sweet potatoes simmered with curry powder, ginger and coconut milk. Creamy without any cream.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the split peas and broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered 30 minutes.
Add the sweet potatoes and simmer 15 to 20 minutes more, until the peas and potatoes are very soft.
Stir in the coconut milk. Blend or mash part of the soup for a thicker texture. Add the lime juice, salt and cilantro.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F with a splash of water.

freezer.text: Freeze for up to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Pack for lunch with a piece of naan or a roll.

recipes.kids: Blend a portion until smooth; most kids like the sweet potato flavor.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth and curry powder labels.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the soup.

recipes.name: Chickpea Curry (Chana Masala)
recipes.summary: Chickpeas simmered in a spiced tomato and onion sauce, served over brown rice. Pantry staples, big flavor.
recipes.serving_size: about 1 cup curry with 3/4 cup rice
steps: Bring the rice and water to a boil, cover, lower the heat and simmer 40 to 45 minutes, until tender. Let stand 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 8 to 10 minutes, until deep golden. Add the garlic, ginger and jalapeño for 1 minute, then the cumin, coriander, paprika and turmeric for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, chickpeas, water and salt. Simmer 15 to 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick. Mash a few chickpeas to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the lemon juice and cilantro. Serve over the rice with yogurt if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: The curry keeps 4 days in the fridge and tastes better on day two. Reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze the curry for up to 3 months.

leftovers.text: Roll leftovers in a warm tortilla with a spoon of yogurt.

recipes.kids: Skip the jalapeño and serve yogurt on the side.

swaps.gluten_free: Already gluten-free; check spice labels.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the curry and the rice.

recipes.name: Crispy Roasted Chickpeas
recipes.summary: Chickpeas roasted until crunchy and tossed with a little salt and smoked paprika. A crunchy snack with protein and fiber.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Pat the chickpeas very dry with a towel and pull off any loose skins.
Toss with the oil and spread in one layer on a baking sheet. Roast 25 to 30 minutes, shaking the pan every 10 minutes, until deep golden and crunchy.
Toss the hot chickpeas with the salt, paprika and garlic powder. Cool on the pan; they crisp more as they cool.
recipes.make_ahead: Best the day they are made. Store loosely covered at room temperature up to 2 days.

freezer.text: They lose their crunch.

leftovers.text: Sprinkle soft leftovers over a salad or soup.

recipes.kids: Try cinnamon and a pinch of sugar instead of paprika. Little ones under 4 should skip them; whole chickpeas can be a choking risk.

prep_day.ahead: Roast a batch for snack bags.

recipes.name: Smashed Chickpea Salad Sandwiches
recipes.summary: Mashed chickpeas with yogurt, celery and lemon, like a tuna salad without the tuna. Ready in 15 minutes.
steps: Mash the chickpeas in a bowl until mostly broken but still chunky.
Stir in the yogurt, mayonnaise, lemon juice, mustard, celery, onion, dill, salt and pepper.
Spread on 4 slices of bread, add lettuce and top with the other slices.
recipes.make_ahead: The filling keeps 4 days in the fridge. Pack it apart from the bread so it does not get soggy.

freezer.text: The filling does not freeze well.

leftovers.text: Scoop the filling onto crackers or into a pita.

recipes.kids: Mash it smoother for small kids and serve in a soft wrap.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free bread or lettuce cups.
swaps.dairy_free: Use all mayonnaise instead of the yogurt.

prep_day.ahead: Mix the filling for the week.

recipes.name: Italian White Bean and Tuna Salad
recipes.summary: Creamy white beans and canned tuna tossed with red onion, celery, parsley and a lemon vinaigrette. A pantry lunch with lots of protein.
steps: Shake the oil, lemon juice, mustard, garlic, salt and pepper in a jar.
In a large bowl, toss the beans, onion, celery, tomatoes and parsley with most of the dressing. Gently fold in the tuna in large flakes.
Serve over the greens with the rest of the dressing.
recipes.make_ahead: The bean and tuna mixture keeps 3 days in the fridge. Add the greens when you serve it.

freezer.text: Does not freeze.

leftovers.text: Stuff leftovers into a pita or spoon onto toast.

recipes.kids: Serve the beans and tuna with crackers, like a tuna salad.

swaps.meatless: Use a third can of beans or chickpeas instead of tuna.

prep_day.ahead: Mix the beans and dressing.

recipes.name: Garlicky White Bean and Herb Dip
recipes.summary: White beans blended with lemon, garlic, parsley and a little rosemary. Serve with vegetables, crackers or bread.
steps: Blend the beans, garlic, lemon juice, olive oil and water until smooth, scraping down the sides.
Add the parsley, rosemary, salt and pepper and pulse until the herbs are finely chopped. Add water if it is too thick.
Spoon into a bowl. It tastes best after 30 minutes in the fridge.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Best fresh.

leftovers.text: Spread it on a sandwich instead of mayonnaise.

recipes.kids: Serve with cucumber rounds, carrot sticks and pita chips.

prep_day.ahead: Make the dip and cut vegetables for snack boxes.

recipes.name: Creamy White Chicken Chili
recipes.summary: Chicken and white beans in a mild green chile broth, made creamy with sour cream and Monterey Jack.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and jalapeño 5 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin and oregano for 30 seconds.
Add the green chiles, broth, chicken breasts and salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until the thickest part of the chicken reaches 165°F.
Lift out the chicken and shred it with 2 forks. Mash 1 can of the beans with a fork and add both cans of beans to the pot. Simmer 5 minutes.
Return the chicken. Off the heat, stir in the sour cream and cheese until melted. Add the cilantro and lime juice.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge. Reheat gently to 165°F so the sour cream does not separate.

freezer.text: Freeze before adding the sour cream and cheese for 2 to 3 months; stir them in after reheating.

leftovers.text: Spoon leftovers over tortilla chips for nachos.

recipes.kids: It is mild; set out tortilla chips to crush on top.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the sour cream and cheese and stir in 1/2 cup coconut milk.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the chili without the dairy.

recipes.name: Pasta e Fagioli
recipes.summary: The Italian-American pasta and bean soup, with a little ground beef, two kinds of beans and small pasta in a tomato broth.
steps: Brown the beef in a large pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F. Spoon off extra fat.
Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 6 minutes. Add the garlic and oregano for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, broth and both beans. Bring to a boil, then simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the pasta and simmer 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until tender. Add the pepper, taste for salt and stir in the basil. Serve with Parmesan.
recipes.make_ahead: The pasta soaks up broth as it sits. To make ahead, cook the pasta separately and add it to each bowl.

freezer.text: Freeze the soup without pasta for up to 3 months.

leftovers.text: Add a splash of broth or water when you reheat it to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids like it with extra Parmesan and a few crackers.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free pasta and check the broth.
swaps.meatless: Skip the beef and use vegetable broth.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the soup base; add pasta when you reheat.

recipes.name: Garden Minestrone
recipes.summary: A big pot of vegetables, beans and small pasta with fresh basil. Use whatever vegetables you have.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery 6 to 8 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the zucchini, green beans, Italian seasoning, tomatoes and broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer 10 minutes.
Add both beans and the pasta. Simmer 8 to 10 minutes, until the pasta is tender.
Stir in the spinach until wilted. Add the pepper, taste for salt and stir in the basil. Serve with Parmesan.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; the pasta keeps soaking up broth, so add water when you reheat it to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze for up to 3 months. For the best texture, freeze it before adding the pasta.

leftovers.text: Pack hot in an insulated food jar for lunch.

recipes.kids: Let kids pick the vegetables at the store. Small pasta shapes make it fun.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free pasta.

prep_day.ahead: Chop the vegetables or cook the whole pot.

recipes.name: Red Beans and Rice
recipes.summary: A weeknight version of the Louisiana classic: red beans, smoked sausage, the "holy trinity" of onion, pepper and celery, and white rice.
recipes.serving_size: about 1 cup beans with 3/4 cup rice
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Brown the sausage 5 minutes; lift it out.
Cook the onion, pepper and celery in the drippings 8 minutes. Add the garlic, thyme, paprika and cayenne for 30 seconds.
Add the beans, broth, bay leaves, pepper and sausage. Simmer uncovered 30 to 35 minutes, stirring often and mashing some beans against the pot, until thick and creamy.
Meanwhile, bring the rice, water and salt to a boil, cover and simmer 18 minutes. Let stand 5 minutes.
Remove the bay leaves. Stir in the green onions and parsley. Serve over rice with hot sauce at the table.
recipes.make_ahead: The beans keep 4 days in the fridge and thicken; add water as you reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze the beans for up to 3 months.

leftovers.text: Wrap leftovers in a tortilla with cheese for a quick burrito.

recipes.kids: Leave out the cayenne and pass hot sauce for the grown-ups.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the sausage and broth labels.
swaps.meatless: Skip the sausage, use vegetable broth and add 1 teaspoon smoked paprika.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the beans and rice.

recipes.name: Three-Bean Salad
recipes.summary: The picnic classic: green beans, kidney beans and chickpeas in a sweet-tart vinaigrette. It gets better as it sits.

ingredients.prep: drained (or 3 cups cooked fresh green beans)

steps: Put the beans, chickpeas, green beans, onion, pepper and parsley in a large bowl.
Shake the vinegar, oil, sugar, salt and pepper in a jar until the sugar dissolves.
Pour over the beans and toss. Cover and chill at least 1 hour, stirring once or twice.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Does not freeze well.

leftovers.text: Spoon it over greens for a quick lunch salad.

recipes.kids: Kids often like the chickpeas best; give them a spoon to fish them out.

prep_day.ahead: Make the salad for the week.

recipes.name: Lentils and Rice with Caramelized Onions (Mujadara)
recipes.summary: A Middle Eastern home dish of lentils and rice, piled with sweet browned onions and served with cool yogurt.
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onions and 1/4 teaspoon salt and cook 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often, until deep brown. Lower the heat if they brown too fast.
Meanwhile, put the lentils in a pot with water to cover by 2 inches. Boil 15 minutes, until just tender, then drain.
Return the lentils to the pot with the rice, cumin, salt, pepper, 3 3/4 cups water and half the onions. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low 18 to 20 minutes. Let stand 10 minutes.
Fluff and top with the remaining onions and the parsley. Serve with yogurt.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Reheat with a splash of water to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze for up to 2 months.

leftovers.text: Serve cold as a salad with cucumbers and tomatoes.

recipes.kids: Kids who like rice usually like this; the onions taste sweet.

swaps.dairy_free: Serve with a dairy-free yogurt, or skip it.

prep_day.ahead: Brown the onions up to 3 days ahead, or cook the whole dish.

recipes.name: Seasoned Lentil Tacos
recipes.summary: Lentils cooked with taco spices until they look and taste like a taco filling. Set out toppings and let everyone build.
steps: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes. Add the garlic, chili powder, cumin, paprika, oregano and salt for 30 seconds, then stir in the tomato paste.

Add the lentils and broth. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer 25 to 30 minutes, until the lentils are tender and most of the liquid is gone. Uncover and cook a few minutes more if it is soupy, mashing a little.
Spoon into warm tortillas and top with cheese, lettuce, tomato and cilantro.
recipes.make_ahead: The filling keeps 5 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze the filling for up to 3 months.

leftovers.text: Use leftover filling in quesadillas or over rice.

recipes.kids: Kids can build their own; offer flour tortillas if they prefer soft and mild.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese and sour cream.
swaps.gluten_free: Corn tortillas are usually gluten-free; check the label and the broth.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the filling and chop the toppings.

recipes.name: Lentil Salad with Feta and Herbs
recipes.summary: Firm lentils tossed with cucumber, feta, parsley and mint in a shallot and mustard dressing. Packs well for lunch.
steps: Cover the lentils and bay leaf with water by 2 inches. Boil, then simmer 18 to 22 minutes, until tender but not mushy. Drain and remove the bay leaf.
While the lentils cook, shake the shallot, vinegar, mustard, oil, salt and pepper in a jar.
Toss the warm lentils with the dressing and let them cool 15 minutes; they soak it up.
Fold in the cucumber, tomatoes, feta, parsley and mint.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Add the herbs and tomatoes the day you serve it for the freshest flavor.

freezer.text: Cucumbers and herbs do not freeze well.

leftovers.text: Stuff it into a pita with lettuce.

recipes.kids: Serve the parts side by side for kids who like their foods separate.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the feta or use a dairy-free crumble.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the lentils and make the dressing.

recipes.name: Lentil Sloppy Joes
recipes.summary: The sweet and tangy sandwich filling kids love, made with lentils instead of beef.
steps: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper 6 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the lentils and water. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer 20 minutes, until the lentils are almost tender.
Stir in the tomato sauce, ketchup, sugar, vinegar, soy sauce, chili powder, mustard and salt. Simmer uncovered 10 to 12 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Spoon onto toasted buns.
recipes.make_ahead: The filling keeps 5 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze the filling for up to 3 months.

leftovers.text: Spoon the filling over a baked potato.

recipes.kids: Serve open-faced with a slice of cheese melted on top.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free buns and tamari instead of soy sauce.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the filling.

recipes.name: Black Bean Soup
recipes.summary: Canned black beans simmered with peppers, cumin and garlic, partly blended and topped with sour cream and cilantro.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, pepper and jalapeño 6 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin and oregano for 30 seconds.
Add the beans, broth and salt. Simmer 10 minutes.
Blend about half the soup (or mash it well) so it is thick but still has whole beans. Stir in the lime juice.
Top each bowl with sour cream and cilantro.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 5 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze without the toppings for up to 3 months.

leftovers.text: Spoon thick leftovers into a quesadilla.

recipes.kids: Set out tortilla chips and shredded cheese as toppings.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the sour cream or use a dairy-free one.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the soup.

recipes.name: Black Bean Burgers
recipes.summary: Hearty bean patties held together with oats and egg, browned in a skillet and finished in the oven.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Spread the beans on a baking sheet and bake 10 minutes to dry them a little. Cool slightly.

Mash the beans in a bowl, leaving some pieces. Pulse the oats in a blender until coarse and add with the egg, pepper, onion, garlic, cilantro, cumin, chili powder and salt. Mix well and shape into 6 patties.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Brown the patties 3 minutes per side.
Move to the baking sheet and bake 8 to 10 minutes, until firm and 160°F in the center. Serve on buns with lettuce and salsa.
recipes.make_ahead: Shape the patties up to 1 day ahead and keep covered in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked patties with wax paper between them for up to 3 months; reheat in a 375°F oven to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Crumble a leftover patty into a burrito bowl.

recipes.kids: Make small slider-size patties; they bake in 6 minutes.

swaps.gluten_free: Use oats labeled gluten-free and gluten-free buns.

prep_day.ahead: Shape and freeze the patties.

recipes.name: Charro Beans
recipes.summary: Pinto beans simmered with bacon, onion, tomato and jalapeño in a savory broth, the way they are served at Tex-Mex cookouts.
steps: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp, about 6 minutes. Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of fat.
Add the onion and jalapeño and cook 5 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the tomatoes for 2 minutes.
Add the beans, broth, cumin, oregano and salt. Simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until the broth is flavorful and a little thick. Stir in the cilantro.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze for up to 3 months.

leftovers.text: Serve leftovers over rice with a fried egg.

recipes.kids: Seed the jalapeño well, or leave it out, for a mild pot.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label.
swaps.meatless: Skip the bacon, cook the onion in oil and use vegetable broth with 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the beans.

recipes.name: Seven-Layer Bean Dip
recipes.summary: Refried beans, seasoned sour cream, guacamole, salsa, cheese, tomatoes and green onions in layers. A party favorite.
steps: Spread the refried beans in the dish.
Stir the sour cream and taco seasoning together and spread over the beans.
Mash the avocados with the lime juice and salt and spread on next. Spoon the salsa over, then sprinkle with cheese, tomato, green onions and olives.
Serve right away with chips, or cover and chill up to 4 hours.
recipes.make_ahead: Layer the beans, sour cream and salsa up to 1 day ahead. Add the avocado and toppings the day of.

freezer.text: Does not freeze.

leftovers.text: Spoon leftovers into a tortilla with rice for a quick burrito. Keep it in the fridge and eat within 2 days.

recipes.kids: Kids can sprinkle the cheese and toppings.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the taco seasoning label; most corn tortilla chips are gluten-free.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free sour cream and skip the cheese.

recipes.name: Edamame Succotash
recipes.summary: A bright, colorful side of edamame, sweet corn and red pepper in butter with fresh basil. A new take on the Southern classic.
steps: Heat the butter and oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper 5 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the edamame, corn and water. Cook, stirring, 5 to 6 minutes, until heated through and tender.
Season with salt, pepper and lemon juice. Stir in the basil.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Good cold as a salad, too.

freezer.text: Best fresh.

leftovers.text: Toss cold leftovers with cooked pasta and a little dressing.

recipes.kids: The colors draw kids in; let them count the different vegetables.

prep_day.ahead: Chop the onion and pepper.

recipes.name: Sesame Garlic Edamame
recipes.summary: Shelled edamame warmed in a skillet with garlic, sesame oil and a splash of soy sauce. A snack ready in 10 minutes.
steps: Cook the edamame in a skillet with 1/4 cup water over medium-high heat, stirring, until the water is gone and they are hot, 4 to 5 minutes.
Add the sesame oil and garlic and stir 1 minute.
Add the soy sauce and sesame seeds and toss. Serve warm or cold.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze the edamame plain instead; it comes frozen.

leftovers.text: Toss leftovers into fried rice or a noodle bowl.

recipes.kids: Pack them cold in a lunchbox with a toothpick for spearing.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari instead of soy sauce.

prep_day.ahead: Make a batch for lunchboxes.

recipes.name: Peanut Noodles with Edamame
recipes.summary: Spaghetti tossed in a creamy peanut sauce with edamame, carrots, cucumber, green onions and cilantro. Eat warm or cold.
steps: Cook the spaghetti in a large pot of boiling salted water by the package directions. Add the edamame for the last 3 minutes. Drain and rinse with cool water.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, vinegar, honey, sesame oil, ginger, garlic and warm water until smooth.
Toss the noodles and edamame with the sauce, carrots, cucumber, green onions and cilantro.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Loosen with a splash of warm water before serving.

freezer.text: The vegetables get soggy.

leftovers.text: Pack cold for lunch; it tastes like takeout.

recipes.kids: Serve the vegetables on the side for picky eaters.

swaps.gluten_free: Use rice noodles or gluten-free spaghetti and tamari.

prep_day.ahead: Make the sauce and shred the vegetables.

recipes.name: Teriyaki Tofu Rice Bowls
recipes.summary: Golden pan-fried tofu in a homemade ginger teriyaki sauce over brown rice with edamame and broccoli.

ingredients.prep: firm, pressed and cut in 1-inch cubes

steps: Bring the rice and water to a boil, cover and simmer on low 40 to 45 minutes. Let stand 10 minutes.
Wrap the tofu in a towel and press with something heavy for 15 minutes. Cut in cubes and toss with 2 tablespoons cornstarch.
Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu, turning, 8 to 10 minutes, until golden on all sides. Move to a plate.
Add the broccoli, edamame and 1/4 cup water to the skillet, cover and steam 4 minutes. Move to the plate.
Whisk the sauce ingredients, pour into the skillet and simmer 1 minute, until glossy. Return the tofu and toss. Serve over rice with the vegetables and green onions.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge in meal-prep containers; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Fried tofu turns spongy when frozen.

leftovers.text: Pack the bowls for lunch and microwave until hot.

recipes.kids: Kids often like the crispy tofu cubes best; serve sauce on the side.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari instead of soy sauce.

prep_day.ahead: Cook rice and tofu; pack 4 bowls.

recipes.name: Crispy Baked Tofu Bites
recipes.summary: Tofu cubes tossed with soy, oil and cornstarch and baked until crisp. Dip them, toss them in sauce or add them to bowls.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment. Wrap the tofu in a towel and press under something heavy for 15 minutes, then cut into 3/4-inch cubes.
Toss the tofu with the soy sauce and oils, then sprinkle with the cornstarch and garlic powder and toss until coated.
Spread in one layer, not touching. Bake 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp at the edges.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Re-crisp in a 400°F oven or air fryer for 5 minutes.

freezer.text: The texture turns spongy.

leftovers.text: Add cold bites to a salad or noodle bowl.

recipes.kids: Serve with ketchup or a sweet dipping sauce; they eat them like nuggets.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari instead of soy sauce.

recipes.name: Veggie Tofu Scramble
recipes.summary: Crumbled tofu cooked with onion, peppers and spinach and tinted gold with turmeric. A hearty egg-free breakfast.
steps: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper 5 minutes.
Crumble the tofu into the pan with your hands, in small and large pieces. Sprinkle with the turmeric, garlic powder, salt and pepper and cook, stirring, 5 minutes, until hot and a little dry.
Stir in the spinach until wilted. Top with cheese if you like and serve with toast.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Best fresh or refrigerated.

recipes.kids: A spoon of ketchup or salsa on top helps first-timers.

recipes.name: Mapo-Style Tofu with Pork
recipes.summary: A family-friendly take on the Sichuan dish: soft tofu and ground pork in a savory garlic, ginger and bean sauce. Mild unless you add heat.

ingredients.prep: sliced, white and green parts separated

steps: Rinse the rice, then simmer it covered in 2 1/4 cups water for 15 minutes. Let stand 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the pork, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F.
Add the garlic, ginger, white parts of the green onions and pepper flakes and stir 1 minute. Stir in the hoisin, soy sauce and broth.
Slide in the tofu and simmer gently 5 minutes, spooning sauce over it without stirring hard. Mix the cornstarch and water, stir it in gently and simmer 1 minute, until glossy.
Drizzle with sesame oil, sprinkle with the green onion tops and serve over rice.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Tofu turns spongy when frozen in sauce.

leftovers.text: Spoon over leftover rice for lunch.

recipes.kids: Leave out the pepper flakes; it tastes like a mild stir-fry sauce.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari and a gluten-free hoisin sauce.
swaps.meatless: Skip the pork and add 8 ounces chopped mushrooms.

recipes.name: Garlic Ginger Tofu and Broccoli Stir-Fry
recipes.summary: Browned tofu, broccoli and peppers in a quick garlic-ginger sauce over jasmine rice.
steps: Rinse the rice, then simmer it covered in 2 1/4 cups water for 15 minutes. Let stand 10 minutes.
Toss the pressed tofu with 1 tablespoon cornstarch. Heat 1 1/2 tablespoons oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown the tofu on all sides, 8 minutes. Move to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil, the broccoli, pepper and 2 tablespoons water. Cover and cook 3 minutes, then uncover and stir-fry 2 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Whisk the sauce ingredients, pour in and stir until thick, about 1 minute. Return the tofu, toss and serve over rice.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Tofu turns spongy when frozen.
